messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Streaming SLOs breached on /v1/generate-stream (pool=gpu-shared-2). p95 up to 870ms, p99 spiking to ~4.5s. Streaming stalls metric increased. Paging oncall team.

oncall-ken: got the page — joining. seeing alerts in dashboard for p99 and stall_count. priya can you list top active tenants on gpu-shared-2?

priya: running quick query against metrics store:
```
SELECT tenant, count(active_streams) as streams, p95, p99, blkio_bytes FROM tenant_metrics WHERE pool='gpu-shared-2' AND ts > now()-5m ORDER BY blkio_bytes DESC LIMIT 15;
```

priya: top hitters: tenant_lyra (blkio bursts, p99 5.2s), tenant-saas-b (p99 2.9s), tenant_dev_9 (short-lived spikes, many small writes). tenant_lyra showing repeated 500MB fsync bursts every ~45s.

zoe: host-level `iostat -x` shows nvme0 avg_lat 180ms during bursts. dstat/reports indicate write queue backing up. suspect aggressive snapshot/checkpoint writes from tenant_lyra.

marc: can we try soft-mitigation: lower blkio.weight for tenant_lyra and set ionice on their long-running processes? also consider temporarily disabling heavy snapshotting via tenant feature-flag if they have snapshot API.

priya: checking cgroup paths:
```
ls /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/pool-gpu-shared-2/
cat /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/pool-gpu-shared-2/tenant_lyra/blkio.weight
# currently 500 (default)
```

priya: applying weight reduction to 100 for tenant_lyra:
```
echo 100 > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/pool-gpu-shared-2/tenant_lyra/blkio.weight
```

priya: also set `ionice -c2 -n7` on pid list for tenant_lyra workers to deprioritize io.

oncall-ken: while that should reduce immediate impact, if tenant keeps triggering bursts we need to move them to dedicated-snapshot pool. can someone open a migration and rule change? router + session manager need updates.

marc: starting migration plan. we'll do a graceful handoff: new sessions -> dedicated-snap-1, drain existing streams with max_grace 8s.

zoe: invoking route change:
```
curl -k -X POST https://router.int/_admin/move-tenant -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' -d '{"tenant":"tenant_lyra","from":"gpu-shared-2","to":"dedicated-snap-1","drain_seconds":8}'
```

zoe: router returned 202. migrating ~48 active streams.

priya: also toggled tenant snapshot flag via admin API to prevent scheduled checkpoints for next 10m while we migrate:
```
POST https://admin.internal/tenants/tenant_lyra/flags
body: {"disable_snapshotting":true, "ttl_seconds":600}
```

jamie: FYI added a temporary QoS rule on host that forces blkio.throttle.read_bps_device for tenant_lyra device to 100MB/s to blunt bursts while migration proceeds.

jamie: command used:
```
echo "8:0 104857600" > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/pool-gpu-shared-2/tenant_lyra/blkio.throttle.read_bps_device
```

zoe: after these three actions (weight reduction, ionice, throttle + admin flag + migration) p95 improved 870ms -> 340ms within 40s. p99 trending down to ~1.4s. streaming stall alerts dropping.

oncall-ken: good. keep the throttle for 5 more minutes after migration completes. can infra open ticket to classify tenant workloads that perform periodic heavy syncs and auto-opt them out of shared pools?

marc: creating INFRA-4907: "Classify and auto-migrate heavy snapshotting tenants from shared pools; add blkio burst alerting." attaching iostat snippets and tenant_lyra traces.

priya: note: kernel dirty settings on hosts were at defaults. temporarily lowered kernel dirty_ratio to 8 and dirty_background_ratio to 4 on impacted hosts to reduce writeback spikes.

priya: commands:
```
echo 8 > /proc/sys/vm/dirty_ratio

echo 4 > /proc/sys/vm/dirty_background_ratio
```

jamie: started a transient node-level change to use `mq-deadline` scheduler on NVMe to reduce tail latency for reads during heavy writes; rolling revert planned in 30m.

zoe: migration finished. tenant_lyra active_streams on gpu-shared-2 are zero. dedicated-snap-1 carrying new connections. p95 now ~310ms, p99 ~1.2s, stall_count back to baseline.

oncall-ken: status update draft to post on status page: "We observed elevated streaming latency due to an unusually heavy snapshot workload from a tenant in a shared GPU pool. We applied IO QoS, temporarily disabled snapshotting, and migrated the tenant to a dedicated snapshot pool. Customer streaming should be restored. No data loss." tagging @support and @trust.

jamie: will follow up with tenant_lyra account team to coordinate permanent adjustments; tenant had scheduled snapshots that were inappropriate for shared pools.

marc: post-incident actions: 1) add per-tenant blkio burst alert (e.g., > X MB/s sustained for 2 minutes) 2) automatic migration rule on detection 3) docs/update best practices for snapshotting on shared pools.

infra-bot: Ticket INFRA-4907 created and assigned to infra-team. Attachments: iostat logs, tenant traces, router audit log. Due: 2026-03-16.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity S3 1: mitigated. Create postmortem PM-INC-4887654321 for follow-up.

oncall-ken: thanks team. owners: infra (marc), runtime (priya), router (zoe), comms (oncall-ken). I'll monitor for 30m and then hand to owners for postmortem.
